name: Four Seasons Paris, George V
positioning: Historic Art Deco palace hotel in Paris's Golden Triangle, steps from the Champs-Élysées
best_for: First-time visitors who want Paris landmarks within walking distance

facts.text: The historic George V hotel was built in 1928 and became a Four Seasons hotel in 1999 after a two-year renovation.
The hotel has 243 rooms: 183 guest rooms and 60 suites, over 8 stories.
The address is 31 avenue George V, 75008 Paris, in the Golden Triangle designer shopping district, bordered by the Champs-Élysées, Avenue Marceau and Avenue Montaigne.
Four Seasons describes the design as historic Art Deco, with classical French furnishings combined with modern contemporary furniture; interior designer Pierre-Yves Rochon.

Four Seasons lists Le Cinq (three Michelin stars, modern French cuisine, Executive Chef Christian Le Squer), L'Orangerie (two Michelin stars) and Le George (one Michelin star, Mediterranean cuisine designed for sharing).
Other dining and drinking venues are the lounge La Galerie and Le Bar.
Le Spa opened in July 2018 with a 17-metre swimming pool, a vitality pool, two hammams, a hair salon and a fitness centre.
The hotel is steps from the Champs-Élysées, Arc de Triomphe, Place de la Concorde and the Eiffel Tower, per Four Seasons.

highlights.text: Le Cinq holds three Michelin stars, with Christian Le Squer as Executive Chef; two more restaurants in the hotel, L'Orangerie and Le George, hold two and one stars.
The hotel sits in the Golden Triangle shopping district, with Avenue Montaigne and the Champs-Élysées as its borders.
The Art Deco building dates to 1928, and the hotel is decorated with fresh flowers (Four Seasons cites 9,000 flowers).
Le Spa has a 17-metre pool, a 34 degree vitality pool and two hammams.

considerations.text: Pricing is ultra-luxury, reflecting the hotel's premium positioning.
The atmosphere is formal and may not suit all travelers.
Le Spa has six treatment rooms, including one couple's suite.
